Low-Budget Repairs Is Out, and It Is a Renovation Sim Set in a 90s Polish Block of Flats

Source Steam and publisher announcement
Out 13 August 2026
Platform PC via Steam
Price US$14.99 at 25% off
Read 2 min
Official key art, via the Low-Budget Repairs Steam store page

A comedy renovation sim about doing dodgy repairs in a 1990s Polish apartment block, out now, and cheap while the launch discount holds.

Low-Budget Repairs landed on Steam on 13 August. You play Maciek, apprenticed to a bloke called Mr Zbyszek, doing repairs in a Polish block of flats in the nineties with whatever is lying around. Gray2RGB developed it, and it is published by Simplicity Games and PlayWay.

On price, the live Steam listing has it at US$14.99 with a 25 per cent launch discount running, which puts the base at US$19.99. The press release we received said 19.69, which does not survive the maths. We could not reach the Australian store to give you a local figure, and we could not find an official end date for the discount, so do not bank on the fourteen days that has been floating about.

The wishlist number is worth being careful with. We have seen 1.2 million quoted. The publisher's own announcements in July and August put it at one million, and that is the number we are going with until someone official says otherwise. Either way it is a lot of people who liked the look of a game about bodging pipework in a stairwell.

It ships in eighteen languages with full Polish and English audio, and there is a free demo on Steam that has been up since late July if you want to try before you spend anything.

One thing the press release left out and Steam does not. The store page carries an AI generated content disclosure from the developers, saying AI was used for some translations, music and visual assets, that the game does not create AI-generated content during gameplay, and that AI was not used to write the code. If that matters to you, and for plenty of people it does, better you hear it here than find it on the store page after you have paid.

The Kropp Take
The setting is the whole reason to look at this. Everyone makes house flipping sims now and they all look like an Ikea catalogue. A crumbling nineties Polish apartment block, with the specific texture of doing a repair job badly because that is what the budget allows, is genuinely different and it is funny before you even press start. Fifteen US dollars is easy money for that. The AI disclosure will be a dealbreaker for some people and I am not going to pretend it is nothing, but the devs put it on the page themselves rather than hiding it, which is more than a lot of studios manage.
On this story
Based on the Low-Budget Repairs Steam store page, publisher announcements from Simplicity Games and PlayWay, and price data cross-checked against GG.deals. Release date 13 August 2026 confirmed on Steam. The US$19.69 base price given in the press release does not reconcile with the live discounted price and has not been used. The one million wishlist figure is the publisher's own stated number. The launch discount end date could not be confirmed.
